name: computer
description: Use a container computer (a Linux desktop with a shared Chromium) from inside it or remotely through its agent API. Run commands as `computer [-c NAME] <name> <arguments...>`; arguments are positional in the listed order, flags go after the command name.

globalFlags.name: -c
globalFlags.description: use the remote NAME (see `computer remote list`); before the command

environment.name: COMPUTER_REMOTE
environment.description: remote to use when -c isn't given

environment.name: COMPUTER_URL
environment.description: computer URL (https://host/alice) to use without a remotes.json; needs COMPUTER_TOKEN

environment.name: COMPUTER_TOKEN
environment.description: agent token for COMPUTER_URL, and the default for `remote add --token`

environment.name: COMPUTER_SETTLE
environment.description: seconds screenshot and zoom wait before capturing (default 0.3)

exitCodes.meaning: error (the message on stderr says what to do next)
usage error (bad command, flag or argument)
exec, shell and desktop actions pass through the exit code of the command on the computer

commands.name: screenshot
commands.description: Takes a PNG screenshot of the whole screen, after a short settle delay (COMPUTER_SETTLE seconds, default 0.3) so the screen reflects your last action. Without FILE, or with -, the PNG goes to stdout. Take one before acting and after, to see what happened; coordinates in the image are screen coordinates.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: where to write the PNG on this machine; - or omitted for stdout

output.description: PNG image bytes on stdout, or nothing when FILE is given (the file is written on this machine)

commands.where: inside a computer it acts locally; elsewhere on the chosen remote (-c NAME)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error; otherwise the exit code of the action on the computer

commands.name: zoom
commands.summary: PNG of a region at full resolution
commands.description: Takes a PNG of just the region from the top-left corner X0 Y0 to the bottom-right corner X1 Y1 (exclusive), at full resolution: use it to read small text or check details. X1 must be greater than X0 and Y1 greater than Y0.

arguments.name: file
arguments.description: where to write the PNG on this machine; - or omitted for stdout

output.description: PNG image bytes on stdout, or nothing when FILE is given (the file is written on this machine)

commands.where: inside a computer it acts locally; elsewhere on the chosen remote (-c NAME)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error; otherwise the exit code of the action on the computer

commands.where: inside a computer it acts locally; elsewhere on the chosen remote (-c NAME)

commands.where: inside a computer it acts locally; elsewhere on the chosen remote (-c NAME)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error; otherwise the exit code of the action on the computer

commands.name: exec
commands.summary: run a command on the computer
commands.description: Runs one command as user (in /workspace unless --cwd) and streams its stdin, stdout and stderr; exits with the command's exit code. The command is run as given, not through a shell: for pipes, globs or && use `-- bash -lc '...'`.

flags.name: --json
flags.description: buffer the output and print one JSON object {"stdout","stderr","exit"} instead of streaming; exit 0 when the JSON was printed

flags.name: --tty
flags.description: run in a terminal (for programs that need one); stdout and stderr are merged

output.description: the command's stdout and stderr as they arrive; with --json one object {"stdout":string,"stderr":string,"exit":int}, using "stdoutBase64"/"stderrBase64" (base64) instead when the output isn't UTF-8

fields.stderrBase64: standard error, base64, when not UTF-8
fields.stdoutBase64: standard output, base64, when not UTF-8

examples: computer exec --json -- bash -lc 'cd app && npm test'
commands.where: on the chosen remote (-c NAME); inside a computer without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the command's own exit code; 1 when it couldn't run (connection, token, stopped computer), 2 usage error

commands.name: shell
commands.description: Opens an interactive bash login shell on the computer in your terminal (raw mode, resizes follow your window). Exit with `exit` or Ctrl-D. For scripted use, prefer exec.
commands.where: on the chosen remote (-c NAME); inside a computer without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: the shell's exit code; 1 when it couldn't start

commands.name: cp
commands.summary: copy files to or from a computer
commands.description: Copies a file or directory between this machine and a computer; write the computer side as NAME:/path (NAME is a remote; an empty NAME, as in :/path, means the chosen remote). A file lands at DST, or inside DST when it is an existing directory. A directory's contents land in DST, which is created (like `cp -r SRC/. DST`). SRC - reads stdin; DST - writes to stdout (a tar stream for a directory). Files land as user; inside a computer, two local paths are copied locally.

output.description: nothing, unless DST is - (the file's bytes or a tar stream)

commands.where: on the chosen remote (-c NAME); inside a computer without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: browser connect
commands.summary: forward the computer's browser to a local CDP port
commands.description: Listens on 127.0.0.1:PORT and forwards the Chrome DevTools Protocol to the computer's shared Chromium (the one on its desktop, with the human's logins), so Playwright, Puppeteer or DevTools tools connect as if the browser were local. Prints the URL, then keeps running until Ctrl-C. Run it in the background. Inside a computer it isn't needed: CDP is at http://127.0.0.1:9221.

output.description: first line: the local CDP URL (http://127.0.0.1:9222); connection log on stderr

commands.where: on the chosen remote (-c NAME); inside a computer without a remote it acts locally
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: remote add
commands.summary: save a computer as a remote
commands.description: Checks the token against the computer's agent API and saves the remote in remotes.json ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/container-computer, default ~/.config/container-computer; mode 0600). URL is the computer's address, like https://host/alice. Tokens come from the computer's Agents tab. The first remote becomes the default.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: local name for the remote (letters, digits, . _ -)

examples: computer remote add alice https://computers.example.com/alice --token cct_…
commands.where: on this machine (no remote needed)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: remote list
commands.description: Lists the saved remotes; * marks the default.

output.description: a table NAME URL TOKEN (token ID only); with --json an array of {name,url,computer,default}

commands.where: on this machine (no remote needed)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: remote remove
commands.description: Removes a saved remote (the token itself stays valid until someone revokes it on the Agents tab).
commands.where: on this machine (no remote needed)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error

commands.name: remote default
commands.summary: set or show the default remote
commands.description: Makes NAME the remote used when no -c or COMPUTER_REMOTE is given; without NAME prints the current default.

output.description: without NAME: the default's name, or nothing

commands.where: on this machine (no remote needed)
commands.exitCodes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error
